about: In communion with the whole Church, the prayer honors the memory of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Saint Joseph, the Apostles, and the martyrs. After naming the saints, it asks God to surround the faithful with His protection through their merits and prayers.

s01.translation: In communion, we venerate the memory above all of the glorious Mary, ever Virgin, Mother of our God and Lord Jesus Christ:

s02.translation: and also blessed Joseph, Spouse of that same Virgin,

s03.translation: and of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs: Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, and Thaddeus;

s04.translation: Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian;

s05.translation: and of all Your Saints; through their merits and prayers, grant that we may be guarded in all things by Your protecting help.

s07.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: A nominative plural participle. Its subject is left unexpressed.

w004.function: Deponent participle governing the chain of genitives that follows.

w009.function: Together with “semper” (w008), Vírginis forms the title ever-Virgin.

w011.function: “Genetríx” means “Mother”. With the genitive “Dei”, the title means “Mother of God”.

w019.function: Together with “sed” (w018), et adds Joseph to the list: but also.

w021.function: An indeclinable name: only “beáti” (w020), which agrees with it, shows the case.

w024.function: A genitive in apposition to “Ioseph” (w021): with the name indeclinable, the case shows in beáti and in Sponsi.

w033.function: The list names twelve Apostles, including Paul rather than Matthias.

w035.function: The first of the two Jameses — the brother of John, son of Zebedee.

w038.function: The second James is the son of Alphaeus. His place in the list distinguishes him from “Iacóbi” (w035).

w045.function: Linus begins the second group of twelve names in this prayer.

w055.function: Saints John and Paul are Roman martyrs commemorated together, not the Apostles named above.

w058.function: Cosmæ and Damiáni are genitives in the list of names dependent on “memóriam” (w003).

w064.function: Ablative plural, which may express cause or means.

w069.function: Neuter: in all things, not among all men.
